purpose: Android platform-capability and capture-health condition identifiers consumed by T-UX-01 and T-QA-12. Every identifier binds to exactly one state of the shared client state taxonomy; Android adds no state of its own.

conditions.description: Automatic capture is paused for a platform reason (force-stop, private-space lock, restricted standby bucket, background restriction) while the rest of the app works. The surface stays fully usable and shows the degraded notice naming automatic capture until capture health is restored.
Automatic capture cannot run because a permission or a restricted setting is not granted. Rendered with the device cause; the recovery action opens the platform's own settings page or prompt.
Any other platform permission or restricted setting reported as not granted. Client-determined; no service result.

reasons.description: The user force-stopped the app. Receivers, jobs and pending intents stay off until the user opens the app again; on Android 15+ pending intents are also cancelled.
reasons.detection: API 35+: ApplicationStartInfo.wasForceStopped() on the first start after the stop decides on its own (true = force-stopped, false = not, whatever the last exit reason says). ApplicationExitInfo.REASON_USER_STOPPED (API 30+, the profile the app ran in was stopped) is honoured on every level. ApplicationExitInfo.REASON_USER_REQUESTED is deliberately not used: Android documents it for a force-stop or a swipe from Recents (before API 34 also an app update) and exposes no public sub-reason, so on API 30-34 a force-stop is not detectable with public APIs; like below API 30, capture health is re-probed at start instead (TrackingPauseDetector).
reasons.limitation: API 30-34: a force-stop cannot be told apart from a swipe from Recents with public APIs and is therefore not reported; the pause is shown only when the platform can say so (API 35+) or when the profile was stopped.
reasons.clears_when: Capture health is restored: the capture components are registered again and a health probe succeeds. A process start alone never clears it.

reasons.description: The private space holding the app was locked, which stops every app inside it and hides its notifications; nothing is captured until the space is unlocked.
reasons.detection: Running in a non-managed profile (UserManager.isProfile() && !isManagedProfile(), API 33+) and the last exit reason was REASON_USER_STOPPED or the start reports wasForceStopped() == true (TrackingPauseDetector). The public SDK cannot name the private space explicitly, so a clone profile is classified the same way.
reasons.clears_when: Capture health is restored after the space is unlocked.
reasons.privacy: Records that the user chose to run the app inside a private space, which is a concealment choice: kept on the device as a per-device state record and a logcat-only event, would only ever be counted in aggregate, never joined to an account identifier, not exported by this baseline, erased with the record by CaptureHealthStore.clear().

reasons.description: The app is in the restricted standby bucket, so jobs run about once a day and the capture pipeline cannot keep up.
reasons.detection: UsageStatsManager.getAppStandbyBucket() == STANDBY_BUCKET_RESTRICTED (45), read by TrackingPauseDetector at process start and reportable at runtime by a drain worker through StopReasonPolicy.captureHealthReason and CaptureHealthMonitor.onPlatformPause.
reasons.clears_when: Capture health is restored: the capture components are registered in the current process and a health probe succeeds, the same path as force_stopped. A process start alone never clears it; while the bucket stays restricted the detector refreshes the reason at each start.

reasons.description: The user applied a background restriction to the app in system settings; background work is not run.
reasons.detection: ActivityManager.isBackgroundRestricted(), read by TrackingPauseDetector at process start and reportable at runtime by a drain worker (STOP_REASON_BACKGROUND_RESTRICTION) through StopReasonPolicy.captureHealthReason and CaptureHealthMonitor.onPlatformPause.
reasons.clears_when: Capture health is restored: the capture components are registered in the current process and a health probe succeeds, the same path as force_stopped. A process start alone never clears it; while the restriction stays the detector refreshes the reason at each start.

reasons.description: Notification access is not granted for the capture listener; the install source is not locked, so the normal settings page enables it.

The restricted-settings matrix says this install source is locked on this API level and the setting is not granted. The rendered copy is the canonical device-cause copy of permission_denied, unchanged; what this reason changes is only the destination of the single review_access action: the app's App info page (where the platform offers Allow restricted settings) instead of the setting's own page.
reasons.detection: Setting not granted and RestrictedSettingsMatrix.availability(installSource, setting, apiLevel).isLocked.
reasons.clears_when: The user unlocks restricted settings for the app and grants the setting, or the build is reinstalled from an unlocked source. Step-by-step unlock guidance is tester documentation (RecoveryPath), not product copy.

reasons.description: A runtime permission capture needs (SMS) is not granted.
reasons.detection: CapturePermissionProbe: ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(context, permission) != PERMISSION_GRANTED for the platform permission the capture feature names; reading requests nothing and shows no prompt. This baseline declares and requests no capture permission, so on this build every capture permission reads as not granted.

capture_health.description: The value android keeps for the capture pipeline. It is not a taxonomy state: healthy renders as content, the other values render through the bound condition.

persisted_record.content: Reason identifiers, one timestamp, one boolean and a platform permission name; never an account identifier, device identifier, package list, transaction or message content.
persisted_record.backup: Excluded from cloud backup and device transfer by res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml and res/xml/backup_rules.xml (allowBackup is false).
persisted_record.erasure: CaptureHealthStore.clear() / CaptureHealthMonitor.clear() removes every key; the sign-out and account-erasure flow of the account ticket calls it so the record, including a private_space_paused indicator and its timestamp, does not outlive the account on the device.

capture_health.erasure_inventory_note: Every artefact android persists for capture health or queued sync is listed in docs/platform/scheduling-and-capture-health.md section 4 (erasure inventory) with its content, backup exclusion, erasure call and export status; this record and the durable queue are the two entries in this baseline.

durable_queue.contract: DurableQueue (platform/scheduling/DurableQueue.kt); reference implementation InMemoryDurableQueue, persisted (Room) form owned by the storage ticket android#6
durable_queue.content: Idempotency keys, timestamps, attempt and lease-expiry counts, dead-letter reason identifiers, and the opaque payloads of pending, in-flight and dead-lettered items, which are transaction content.
durable_queue.diagnostics: QueuedItem.toString() and DeadLetter.toString() never include the payload.
durable_queue.erasure: DurableQueue.clear() removes pending, in-flight and dead-lettered items with their payloads regardless of leases; the sign-out and account-erasure flow calls it. The queue itself deletes nothing else; the storage ticket owns retention of the persisted form.
durable_queue.export: None: no export of a queued or parked item exists in this baseline; any future export names its purpose and retention first.

observability.note: The taxonomy signal client_state.<identifier> keeps exactly the published attributes; the condition and reason travel in android's own capture_health log event, not in the signal. private_space_paused is counted locally and in aggregate only and is never joined to an account identifier.
observability.sink: Local Log.i with tag PenniLogic only; no telemetry export exists in this baseline. Any future export names its purpose, aggregation and retention here first.
observability.retention: The device logcat ring buffer; nothing is persisted by the app for this event.

implementation.description: Where the identifiers are produced; paths are relative to app/src/main/kotlin/com/pennilogic/android/ and ClientStateTaxonomyTest asserts they exist.

requests_to_taxonomy_owner: Record the seven reason identifiers above as the published platform-capability identifiers under capture_paused_by_platform and capture_blocked_by_setting (PenniLogic/docs#1 definition of done, item 3).
Confirm that the capture surface's {capability} placeholder value is 'Automatic capture' and its {permission} values are the platform permission names listed in the restricted-settings matrix.

If product copy should guide the user through the restricted-settings unlock step by step, add that guidance to the taxonomy (a device-cause variant or a placeholder) first; until then restricted_setting_locked only changes the review_access destination.
